problem:
Consider the vector $x$ and the subspace $S=\text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 5 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -4 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,\,x=[\begin{aligned}20 \\ -20 \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ given that the set ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ is orthogonal.

feedback.problem:
Consider the vector $x$ and the subspace $S=\text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}},$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0 \\ 2 \\ -2\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ -1 \\ -2\end{aligned}],\,\,x=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1 \\ -3 \\ -12\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ given that the set ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}}$ is orthogonal.
feedback.worked_solution:
Since the set ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}}$ is orthogonal, the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x={\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{3}}x.
$$

So, we first find the orthogonal projections of $x$ onto $\text{Span}{{a}_{1}},$ $\text{Span}{{a}_{2}},$ and $\text{Span}{{a}_{3}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{1}}{{a}_{1}\cdot {a}_{1}}{a}_{1}=\frac{0\cdot (-1)+(-1)\cdot 0+(-3)\cdot 2+(-12)\cdot (-2)}{(-1)^{2}+{0}^{2}+{2}^{2}+(-2)^{2}}{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 0 \\ 4 \\ -4\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{2}}{{a}_{2}\cdot {a}_{2}}{a}_{2}=\frac{0\cdot 2+(-1)\cdot 0+(-3)\cdot 2+(-12)\cdot 1}{{2}^{2}+{0}^{2}+{2}^{2}+{1}^{2}}{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 0 \\ -4 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{{a}_{3}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{3}}{{a}_{3}\cdot {a}_{3}}{a}_{3}=\frac{0\cdot 2+(-1)\cdot 0+(-3)\cdot (-1)+(-12)\cdot (-2)}{{2}^{2}+{0}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+(-2)^{2}}{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 0 \\ -3 \\ -6\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & ={\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{3}}x \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 0 \\ 4 \\ -4\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 0 \\ -4 \\ -2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 0 \\ -3 \\ -6\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ -3 \\ -12\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
